findings_qualitative.value: Outer disk emission at 60-110 au found at 0.65, 0.87 and 1.3 mm but not at 2.1 and 3.1 mm

evidence.quote: However, we do not recover any outer-disk emission at 2.1 mm and 3.1 mm to the noise level.

claims.hypothesis: Faint substructure exists in TW Hya's outer disk at multiple wavelengths
claims.experiment: Image-plane profiles at Bands 6,7; visibility fits at Band 8
claims.result: D79/B86 at 0.87 and 1.3 mm; quasi-constant emission with D86/B96 at 0.65 mm
claims.finding: A faint outer ring exists, consistent with Ilee et al.

evidence.quote: With image-plane retrieval, our 0.87 mm and 1.3 mm observations resolve substructures in the R $\geq$ 60 au of TW Hya, namely D79 and B86.

claims.hypothesis: Outer ring dust is small grains
claims.finding: Optically thin, grains much smaller than 1 mm

evidence.quote: This may indicate dust grains that are optically thin and much smaller than 1 mm in size

why_this_method.value: Azimuthally averaged profiles showed no substructure at Band 8, so visibility-plane fitting was used

evidence.quote: On azimuthally averaging the intensity obtained from the continuum image, we were not able to detect any substructures.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Normal frank method rejected in favor of logNormal for fewer noise artifacts

evidence.quote: We direct our focus to the logNormal profiles since they contain fewer noise-induced artifacts.

limitations_admitted.value: Band 8 resolution insufficient to resolve the substructure; large location uncertainties

evidence.quote: higher angular resolution ALMA Band 8 observations (at least $\sim$ 0.1”, 6 au), with high sensitivity and S/N, are required to resolve the separation and morphology of this substructure.

referee_caveats_inferred: Outer ring at Band 8 is only ~1 sigma; Gaussian ring model choice drives detection
Frank logNormal shows a shoulder rather than a ring, model dependent
Optically thin single-temperature (20 K) mass is uncertain; opacity law not tested
Spectral index mixes image-plane and model-derived fluxes at different resolutions
